newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 23.86 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 23.86 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs VE6MTMA=RR rose 233 basis points to 23.86 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 58 billion bolivars of 178- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 21.53 percent coupon for a price of 98.97. Eighty billion bolivars of paper was offered. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 21.53 percent

The bank also sold 19 billion bolivars of 269-day notes VE9MTMA=RR with a 22.11 percent coupon at a price of 97.93 percent, and 28 billion bolivars of 358-day notes VE1YTMA=RR with a 22.69 percent coupon at an average price of 96.99 percent.
Thirty billion bolivars at each maturity were offered.
Yields for these notes rose 188 basis points to 25.41 percent for the 269-day bills, and 211 basis points to 26.52 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
